f.title: Report all SUSARs in line with applicable requirements and ICH E2A
f.statement: Reporting of all suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions (SUSARs) shall comply with all applicable regulatory requirements and the ICH Guideline for Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting (ICH E2A), which the Order adopts (Annex C).
f.applicability: All clinical trials of investigational products covered by the Order (Section III scope, incl. trials of authorised products for new indications/populations/risk assessment)

rows.quote: Reporting of all Suspected, Unexpected Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR) shall comply with all applicable regulatory requirements and the ICH Guideline for Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting (ICH E2A) which is hereby adopted (Annex C).

f.title: Sponsor or CRO expedites SUSAR reporting to FDA per ICH E2A
f.statement: The sponsor or the CRO is responsible for expedited reporting of all SUSARs to the FDA in accordance with the Standards for Expedited Reporting of ICH E2A.

rows.quote: The sponsor to the FDA, or in the CRO is responsible for expediting the reporting of all SUSARs accordance with the Standards for Expedited Reporting of the ICH Guideline for Clinical Safety Data Management: Definitions and Standards for Expedited Reporting (ICH E2A).

f.title: Code adverse reactions with MedDRA
f.statement: MedDRA terminology shall be used in coding the adverse reaction(s) in SUSAR reports.

rows.quote: The terminology recommended by the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) term shall be used in coding the adverse reaction(s).

f.title: Notify FDA of fatal or life-threatening SUSARs within 7 calendar days
f.statement: For fatal or life-threatening unexpected adverse reactions, the FDA shall be notified as soon as possible but no later than seven calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies.
f.clause: VI.6.1.1.1 Fatal or Life-Threatening Unexpected Adverse Reaction

deadline_rule.clock_start: first knowledge by the sponsor that a case qualifies

f.title: Submit a complete fatal/life-threatening SUSAR report within 8 additional calendar days
f.statement: The 7-day notification of a fatal or life-threatening SUSAR shall be followed by as complete a report as possible within eight additional calendar days. This report shall include an assessment of the importance and implication of the findings, including relevant previous experience with the same or similar medicinal products.
f.clause: VI.6.1.1.1 Fatal or Life-Threatening Unexpected Adverse Reaction

f.title: File other SUSARs within 15 calendar days
f.statement: Serious, unexpected adverse reactions that are not fatal or life-threatening shall be filed as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after first knowledge by the sponsor that the case meets the minimum criteria for expedited reporting.
f.clause: VI.6.1.1.2 All Other Serious, Unexpected Adverse Reaction

f.title: Report a reaction later determined to be a fatal/life-threatening SUSAR within 7 days
f.statement: If the results of a sponsor's investigation show that an adverse reaction not initially determined to be reportable is reportable as a SUSAR, the sponsor and/or CRO shall report it as soon as possible but no later than seven calendar days after the determination is made for fatal or life-threatening unexpected ADRs.

rows.deadline: No later than 7 calendar days after the determination is made
rows.quote: If the results of a sponsor’s investigation show that an adverse reaction not initially determined to be reportable under the identified expedited reporting is reportable as a SUSAR, the sponsor and/or CRO shall report such as soon as possible but in no case later than seven calendar days (Fatal or Life-Threatening Unexpected ADR) or 15 calendar days (All Other Serious, Unexpected ADRs) after the determination is made.

f.title: Report a reaction later determined to be another SUSAR within 15 days
f.statement: If a sponsor's investigation shows that an adverse reaction not initially determined to be reportable is reportable as a SUSAR that is not fatal or life-threatening, the sponsor and/or CRO shall report it as soon as possible but no later than 15 calendar days after the determination is made.

f.title: Include local expected SAEs in the interim/annual report
f.statement: Local expected serious adverse events (SAEs) shall be included in the interim/annual report.

rows.quote: Local expected serious adverse event (SAE) shall be included in the Interim/Annual Report.

f.title: Submit the DSUR annually based on the DIBD
f.statement: The Development Safety Update Report (DSUR) shall be submitted annually, following the month and year of the Development International Birth Date (DIBD).

rows.deadline: Annually, following the month and year of the DIBD

f.title: Submit safety reports with a cover letter and DSUR executive summary with SAR line listings
f.statement: Documentary requirements for safety reporting are: a cover letter (Appendix D2) and the DSUR executive summary, supplemented with line listings of serious adverse reactions (SARs), as appropriate.
f.clause: Appendix D Other Documentary Requirements, I.B Safety Reporting

f.title: Include the required data in the safety-report cover letter
f.statement: For safety reports, the cover letter must include the report identification or manufacturing control number, the description of the SUSAR or event term, report status (initial or follow-up), date of the report, outcome of the event and assessment; for a DSUR, a description of the report. The letter references the full trial title, clinical trial approval number and protocol number.
f.clause: Appendix D2 Cover Letter (Safety Reporting/DSUR/Annual Progress Report/Termination)

f.title: Submit an annual study progress report by the end of the second quarter
f.statement: The sponsor or CRO shall submit a study progress report annually to the FDA (within the second quarter of the year, ending on 30 June), provided the clinical trial has been approved for at least 12 months, until the study ends. An interim report should be submitted for each protocol (format in Appendix G).
f.applicability: Trials approved for at least 12 months, until the study ends

rows.deadline: Annually, within the second quarter (by 30 June)
rows.quote: The sponsor or CRO shall submit a study progress report annually (within the second quarter of the year ending on June 30) to the FDA, provided that the clinical trial has been approved for at least 12 months, until the study ends. An interim report should be submitted for each protocol.
rows.review_note: Review: kept because the annual report carries local expected SAEs (6.3) and the SUSAR section of Appendix G. Recurring date, so no deadline_rule. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Annual report: give a SUSAR line listing and explain any late SUSAR notification
f.statement: In the interim/annual report, the sponsor must state whether there have been any SUSARs in the trial and, if yes, include the line listing of SUSARs; it must state whether these SUSARs were notified to the FDA within 7/15 days under ICH E2A and, if not, arrange notification urgently and give reasons for late notification.
f.clause: Appendix G Interim/Annual Report format - Safety Reports

f.title: Submit urgent-safety protocol deviations and reasons as soon as possible
f.statement: The investigator may implement a deviation from, or a change of, the protocol to eliminate an immediate hazard to trial subjects without prior approval/favourable opinion. As soon as possible, the implemented deviation or change, the reasons for it and, if appropriate, the proposed protocol amendment(s) should be submitted.

rows.quote: As soon as possible, the implemented deviation or change, the reasons for it, and, if appropriate, the proposed protocol amendment(s) should be submitted.

f.title: Give FDA access to trial records and submit them on written request
f.statement: The sponsor, CRO or investigator shall be responsible for securing agreement from all involved parties so that the FDA, for inspection and verification, can access (and if needed copy) any records and reports relating to a clinical trial; upon written request by the FDA, they shall submit the records or reports (or copies) to the FDA.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Data integrity & records

rows.quote: The sponsor, CRO or the investigator shall be responsible for securing agreement from all involved parties to ensure that FDA, for the purpose of inspection and verification, can have access to (and if needed, obtain copies of) any records and reports relating to a clinical trial conducted. Also, upon written request by FDA, the sponsor, CRO or the investigator shall submit the recordsor reports (or copies of them) to FDA.
rows.review_note: Review: record-keeping duty kept; other inspection logistics out of the safety-only scope. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Retain all trial documents for the required period
f.statement: All documents related to the trial shall be retained by the sponsor, CROs and investigator at least two years after the last approval of a marketing application and until there are no pending or contemplated marketing applications; or at least two years after formal discontinuation of clinical development of the investigational product; and/or five years after completion of the clinical trial.

rows.deadline: Retention: at least 2 years after last marketing approval / discontinuation of development, and/or 5 years after trial completion
rows.quote: All documents related to the trial shall be retained by the sponsor, CROs and investigator at least two years after the last approval of a marketing application and until there are no pending or contemplated marketing applications; or at least two years have elapsed since the formal discontinuation of clinical development of the investigational product; and/or five years after the completion of the clinical trial.
rows.review_note: Review: retention periods, not a submission deadline; no deadline_rule. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Apply the SUSAR definition using the reference safety information
f.statement: A SUSAR is a serious adverse reaction whose nature, severity or outcome is not consistent with the reference safety information (e.g. investigator's brochure for an investigational product or summary of product characteristics for an authorised product).
f.processes: Clinical safety monitoring; Case processing & follow-up

rows.quote: Suspected, Unexpected, Serious Adverse Reaction (SUSAR): a serious adverse reaction, the nature, severity or outcome of which is not consistent with the reference safety information (e.g. investigator's brochure for investigational product or summary of product characteristics for authorized product).
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it decides expedited reportability. Double-check: confirmed.
